fluff.overview:
The Model 97 'Octopus' is a fifteen-thousand-ton Spheroid DropShip designed to serve as an interplanetary tug and rescue-salvage vessel. Introduced in 3051 as a successor to the Star League era Model 96 'Elephant,' the Octopus was built from the ground up to tow vessels far larger than itself, including disabled DropShips, JumpShips, and even smaller WarShips.

Though classified as a civilian design, the Octopus carries a surprisingly high level of weaponry and armor for a tug, which its manufacturer insists is merely prudent for a vessel that routinely operates alone in hostile or contested territory. This level of protection has led military observers to speculate that the design may also be intended as an oversized boarding vessel, a capability the manufacturer has neither confirmed nor denied.
fluff.capabilities:
The Octopus is built around a brand-new six-thousand-ton Merlin interplanetary drive that provides a maximum thrust of 4.5 Gs, allowing the vessel to maintain nearly half a G when towing the largest DropShips, JumpShips, or smaller WarShips. The nose features a sophisticated tug adapter and eight articulated arms that securely attach to any vessel, including those without docking collars. A universal airlock adapter fits tight against any target hull, with cutting equipment to force entry during salvage or rescue operations.

Defensive armament is distributed across all arcs. The nose mounts an ER large laser, two medium lasers, an LRM-10 with Artemis IV fire control, and a large pulse laser. Each side carries an identical battery supplemented by two additional large lasers and two medium lasers. The aft arc mounts an ER large laser, two medium lasers, and an LRM-10 with Artemis IV. One hundred and ninety-nine single heat sinks manage the thermal load. Four small craft bays support shuttling operations, and nearly 4,800 tons of cargo space accommodates salvaged materials. Eight infantry bays allow the vessel to carry boarding or security detachments. Four permanently fixed landing legs allow planetary landings, though the vessel's operational profile rarely calls for them.
fluff.deployment: The Model 97 'Octopus' serves in both civilian and military fleets across the Inner Sphere, performing heavy towing, salvage, and rescue operations. Its ability to recover disabled vessels under hostile conditions has made it a valued asset for naval commands operating in contested systems, while civilian operators prize its unmatched towing capacity for commercial salvage work.
fluff.history:
The Model 97 'Octopus' was developed by Nimakachi Fusion Products Limited as an evolution of the Star League era Model 96 'Elephant' tug design. Entering production in 3051, the Octopus was purpose-built to address the growing need for heavy towing and salvage capability in the post-Clan Invasion era, when damaged WarShips and DropShips littered the approaches to numerous worlds. The availability of recovered Star League technology allowed Nimakachi to incorporate advanced components that the original Elephant design had lacked.

The vessel's heavy armament and robust construction have made it attractive to both civilian salvage operators and military commands seeking a vessel capable of recovering damaged assets under fire. The Octopus's ability to forcibly dock with disabled or derelict vessels gives it a secondary boarding capability that has not gone unnoticed by naval planners across the Inner Sphere, though Nimakachi has consistently marketed the design as a purely civilian product.
